sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca punar eveha me buddhiḥ saṃśaye parimuhyate apāre mārgamāṇasya paraṃ tīram apaśyataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Once again my mind is bewildered here, sunk in doubt, like one searching across a shoreless flood who can see no farther bank.

sanskrit: vedāḥ pratyakṣam ācāraḥ pramāṇaṃ tat trayaṃ yadi pṛthaktvaṃ labhyate caiṣāṃ dharmaś caikas trayaṃ katham
english: The Vedas, direct perception, and established custom—these three are authoritative. If a difference is found among them, yet dharma is one, how can it be threefold?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca dharmasya hriyamāṇasya balavadbhir durātmabhiḥ yady evaṃ manyase rājaṃs tridhā dharmavicāraṇā
english: Bhīṣma said: O king, when dharma is being carried off by the powerful and evil-minded, if you think thus, then the inquiry into dharma proceeds along three paths.

sanskrit: eka eveti jānīhi tridhā tasya pradarśanam pṛthaktve caiva me buddhis trayāṇām api vai tathā
english: Know it to be but one; its display is threefold. And my judgment too holds the same about the distinctness of these three.

sanskrit: ukto mārgas trayāṇāṃ ca tat tathaiva samācara jijñāsā tu na kartavyā dharmasya paritarkaṇāt
english: The path of the three has been declared; act accordingly. No quibbling inquiry should be made by over-reasoning about dharma.

sanskrit: sadaiva bharataśreṣṭha mā te bhūd atra saṃśayaḥ andho jaḍa ivāśaṅko yad bravīmi tad ācara
english: Always, O best of the Bharatas, let there be no doubt in you here. Trusting like a blind, dull man, do what I tell you.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā satyam akrodho dānam etac catuṣṭayam ajātaśatro sevasva dharma eṣa sanātanaḥ
english: Non-violence, truth, freedom from anger, and giving—cultivate this fourfold practice, O Ajātaśatru; this is the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇeṣu ca vṛttir yā pitṛpaitāmahocitā tām anvehi mahābāho svargasyaite hi deśikāḥ
english: And the conduct toward Brāhmaṇas that befits your fathers and forefathers—follow that, O mighty-armed one; for these are the guides to heaven.

sanskrit: pramāṇam apramāṇaṃ vai yaḥ kuryād abudho naraḥ na sa pramāṇatām arho vivādajanano hi saḥ
english: The foolish man who would make the authoritative unauthoritative does not deserve to be deemed authoritative himself, for he is a breeder of dispute.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇān eva sevasva satkṛtya bahumanya ca eteṣv eva tv ime lokāḥ kṛtsnā iti nibodha tān
english: Serve the Brāhmaṇas alone, honoring and esteeming them greatly; know that in them rest all these worlds entire.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ye ca dharmam asūyanti ye cainaṃ paryupāsate bravītu bhagavān etat kva te gacchanti tādṛśāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Those who revile dharma and those who wait upon it—let your reverence tell me this: where do such men go?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca rajasā tamasā caiva samavastīrṇacetasaḥ narakaṃ pratipadyante dharmavidveṣiṇo narāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Men whose minds are wholly overspread by passion and darkness, who hate dharma, fall into hell.

sanskrit: ye tu dharmaṃ mahārāja satataṃ paryupāsate satyārjavaparāḥ santas te vai svargabhujo narāḥ
english: But those, O great king, who ever attend upon dharma, devoted to truth and uprightness—those good men are the enjoyers of heaven.

sanskrit: dharma eva ratis teṣām ācāryopāsanād bhavet devalokaṃ prapadyante ye dharmaṃ paryupāsate
english: Their delight is in dharma itself, arising from service to the teacher; those who wait upon dharma attain the world of the gods.

sanskrit: manuṣyā yadi vā devāḥ śarīram upatāpya vai dharmiṇaḥ sukham edhante lobhadveṣavivarjitāḥ
english: Whether men or gods, the righteous who have mortified the body and are freed from greed and hatred flourish in happiness.

sanskrit: prathamaṃ brahmaṇaḥ putraṃ dharmam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ dharmiṇaḥ paryupāsante phalaṃ pakvam ivāśayaḥ
english: The wise call Dharma the firstborn son of Brahmā; the righteous attend upon it as the storehouse cherishes ripened fruit.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca asatāṃ kīdṛśaṃ rūpaṃ sādhavaḥ kiṃ ca kurvate bravītu me bhavān etat santo 'santaś ca kīdṛśāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What is the character of the wicked, and what do the good do? Let your honor tell me this: of what sort are the good and the bad?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca durācārāś ca durdharṣā durmukhāś cāpy asādhavaḥ sādhavaḥ śīlasaṃpannāḥ śiṣṭācārasya lakṣaṇam
english: Bhīṣma said: The wicked are ill-behaved, unapproachable, and foul-mouthed; the good are endowed with virtue—such is the mark of cultivated conduct.

sanskrit: rājamārge gavāṃ madhye goṣṭhamadhye ca dharmiṇaḥ nopasevanti rājendra sargaṃ mūtrapurīṣayoḥ
english: On the highway, amid cattle, and within the cow-pen the righteous do not, O lord of kings, indulge in the discharge of urine and excrement.

sanskrit: pañcānām aśanaṃ dattvā śeṣam aśnanti sādhavaḥ na jalpanti ca bhuñjānā na nidrānty ārdrapāṇayaḥ
english: Having given food to the five, the good eat what remains; while eating they do not chatter, nor do they sleep with hands still wet.

sanskrit: citrabhānum anaḍvāhaṃ devaṃ goṣṭhaṃ catuṣpatham brāhmaṇaṃ dhārmikaṃ caityaṃ te kurvanti pradakṣiṇam
english: The fire, the ox, a deity, the cow-pen, a crossroads, a righteous Brāhmaṇa, and a sacred shrine—these they circumambulate to the right.

sanskrit: vṛddhānāṃ bhārataptānāṃ strīṇāṃ bālāturasya ca brāhmaṇānāṃ gavāṃ rājñāṃ panthānaṃ dadate ca te
english: To the aged, to the burdened, to women, to the child and the sick, to Brāhmaṇas, to cattle, and to kings they yield the path.

sanskrit: atithīnāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ preṣyāṇāṃ svajanasya ca tathā śaraṇakāmānāṃ goptā syāt svāgatapradaḥ
english: Of all guests, of servants, and of one's own kin, and of those who seek refuge, one should be a protector and a bestower of welcome.

sanskrit: sāyaṃ prātar manuṣyāṇām aśanaṃ devanirmitam nāntarā bhojanaṃ dṛṣṭam upavāsavidhir hi saḥ
english: Evening and morning is the meal of men ordained by the gods; no eating between is prescribed—that indeed is the rule of fasting.

sanskrit: homakāle yathā vahniḥ kālam eva pratīkṣate ṛtukāle tathā nārī ṛtum eva pratīkṣate na cānyāṃ gacchate yas tu brahmacaryaṃ hi tat smṛtam
english: As fire at the time of oblation awaits only its due time, so a wife awaits only her season; and he who goes to no other woman—that is remembered as celibacy.

sanskrit: amṛtaṃ brāhmaṇā gāva ity etat trayam ekataḥ tasmād gobrāhmaṇaṃ nityam arcayeta yathāvidhi
english: The nectar of immortality, Brāhmaṇas, and cows—these three are as one; therefore one should always honor cow and Brāhmaṇa according to the rule.

sanskrit: yajuṣā saṃskṛtaṃ māṃsam upabhuñjan na duṣyati pṛṣṭhamāṃsaṃ vṛthāmāṃsaṃ putramāṃsaṃ ca tat samam
english: One does not sin by eating flesh consecrated with the sacrificial formula; but flesh from the back, flesh taken in vain, and the flesh of one's son are all alike.

sanskrit: svadeśe paradeśe vāpy atithiṃ nopavāsayet karma vai saphalaṃ kṛtvā gurūṇāṃ pratipādayet
english: Whether in one's own land or in a foreign land, one should not let a guest go fasting; having performed an act fruitfully, one should dedicate it to the elders.

sanskrit: gurubhya āsanaṃ deyam abhivādyābhipūjya ca gurūn abhyarcya vardhante āyuṣā yaśasā śriyā
english: A seat should be offered to elders, with salutation and honor; by worshiping elders men increase in life, in fame, and in fortune.

sanskrit: vṛddhān nātivadej jātu na ca saṃpreṣayed api nāsīnaḥ syāt sthiteṣv evam āyur asya na riṣyate
english: One should never speak harshly to elders, nor send them on errands, nor remain seated while they stand—thus his life is not diminished.

sanskrit: na nagnām īkṣate nārīṃ na vidvān puruṣān api maithunaṃ satataṃ guptam āhāraṃ ca samācaret
english: The wise man does not gaze upon a naked woman, nor even upon naked men; he should keep both union and eating ever private.

sanskrit: tīrthānāṃ guravas tīrthaṃ śucīnāṃ hṛdayaṃ śuci darśanānāṃ paraṃ jñānaṃ saṃtoṣaḥ paramaṃ sukham
english: Among sacred fords, the elders are the holy ford; among the pure, the heart is the purifier; among insights, knowledge is supreme; contentment is the highest happiness.

sanskrit: sāyaṃ prātaś ca vṛddhānāṃ śṛṇuyāt puṣkalā giraḥ śrutam āpnoti hi naraḥ satataṃ vṛddhasevayā
english: Evening and morning one should listen to the abundant words of elders; for a man attains learning by constant service to elders.

sanskrit: svādhyāye bhojane caiva dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇim uddharet yacched vāṅmanasī nityam indriyāṇāṃ ca vibhramam
english: In recitation and in eating one should raise the right hand; one should ever restrain speech and mind and the wandering of the senses.

sanskrit: saṃskṛtaṃ pāyasaṃ nityaṃ yavāgūṃ kṛsaraṃ haviḥ aṣṭakāḥ pitṛdaivatyā vṛddhānām abhipūjanam
english: Consecrated milk-rice, gruel, sesame-and-rice, and oblation, the Aṣṭaka rites belonging to the ancestral deities, and the honoring of elders—these are duties.

sanskrit: śmaśrukarmaṇi maṅgalyaṃ kṣutānām abhinandanam vyādhitānāṃ ca sarveṣām āyuṣaḥ pratinandanam
english: There is auspicious blessing at the trimming of the beard, a greeting for those who sneeze, and for all the sick a wish of long life in return.

sanskrit: na jātu tvam iti brūyād āpanno 'pi mahattaram tvaṃkāro vā vadho veti vidvatsu na viśiṣyate avarāṇāṃ samānānāṃ śiṣyāṇāṃ ca samācaret
english: One should never say 'thou' to a greater man, even when in distress; among the learned, the familiar 'thou' is reckoned no better than a blow. Such address one may use toward inferiors, equals, and pupils.

sanskrit: pāpam ācakṣate nityaṃ hṛdayaṃ pāpakarmiṇām jñānapūrvaṃ vinaśyanti gūhamānā mahājane
english: The heart of evildoers ever betrays their sin; knowingly they perish, though they conceal it before the multitude.

sanskrit: jñānapūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ karma cchādayante hy asādhavaḥ na māṃ manuṣyāḥ paśyanti na māṃ paśyanti devatāḥ pāpenābhihataḥ pāpaḥ pāpam evābhijāyate
english: The wicked conceal a deed done knowingly, thinking 'men do not see me, the gods do not see me'; but the sinner, struck down by his sin, is reborn only as sin.

sanskrit: yathā vārdhuṣiko vṛddhiṃ dehabhede pratīkṣate dharmeṇāpihitaṃ pāpaṃ dharmam evābhivardhayet
english: As a usurer awaits his increase until the breaking of the body, so sin concealed beneath dharma only makes dharma itself grow.

sanskrit: yathā lavaṇam ambhobhir āplutaṃ pravilīyate prāyaścittahataṃ pāpaṃ tathā sadyaḥ praṇaśyati
english: As salt drenched in water dissolves away, so sin, struck down by expiation, at once perishes.

sanskrit: tasmāt pāpaṃ na gūheta gūhamānaṃ vivardhate kṛtvā tu sādhuṣv ākhyeyaṃ te tat praśamayanty uta
english: Therefore one should not hide a sin, for when hidden it increases; having committed it, one should confess it among the good, and they indeed allay it.

sanskrit: āśayā saṃcitaṃ dravyaṃ yat kāle nopabhujyate anye caitat prapadyante viyoge tasya dehinaḥ
english: The wealth heaped up in hope that is not enjoyed in its time—others come to possess it at the embodied one's parting.

sanskrit: mānasaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ dharmam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni dharmam eva samāsate
english: The wise call dharma the inner disposition of all beings; therefore all beings rest in dharma alone.

sanskrit: eka eva cared dharmaṃ na dharmadhvajiko bhavet dharmavāṇijakā hy ete ye dharmam upabhuñjate
english: Alone one should practice dharma, and not become a parader of dharma; for they are traffickers in dharma who make a living off it.

sanskrit: arced devān adambhena sevetāmāyayā gurūn nidhiṃ nidadhyāt pāratryaṃ yātrārthaṃ dānaśabditam
english: One should worship the gods without ostentation and serve elders without deceit; one should lay up a treasure for the world beyond—called charity—for the sake of the onward journey.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca nābhāgadheyaḥ prāpnoti dhanaṃ subalavān api bhāgadheyānvitas tv arthān kṛśo bālaś ca vindati
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: A man without his portion of fate gains no wealth, however strong he be; but one blessed with his destined share, though feeble and a child, comes by riches.

sanskrit: nālābhakāle labhate prayatne 'pi kṛte sati lābhakāle 'prayatnena labhate vipulaṃ dhanam kṛtayatnāphalāś caiva dṛśyante śataśo narāḥ
english: In a time of non-gain one gains nothing even when effort is made; in a time of gain, without effort, one obtains abundant wealth. And by the hundreds men are seen whose efforts bear no fruit.

sanskrit: yadi yatno bhaven martyaḥ sa sarvaṃ phalam āpnuyāt nālabhyaṃ copalabhyeta nṛṇāṃ bharatasattama
english: If effort were decisive, a mortal would gain every fruit, and nothing unattainable would remain unattained for men, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: yadā prayatnaṃ kṛtavān dṛśyate hy aphalo naraḥ mārgan nayaśatair arthān amārgaṃś cāparaḥ sukhī
english: For one man is seen fruitless though he has made effort, seeking wealth by a hundred prudent ways; while another, taking no proper course at all, is happy.

sanskrit: akāryam asakṛt kṛtvā dṛśyante hy adhanā narāḥ dhanayuktās tv adharmasthā dṛśyante cāpare janāḥ
english: Some men are seen poor though they have done forbidden deeds again and again; while others, set in unrighteousness, are seen possessed of wealth.

sanskrit: adhītya nītiṃ yasmāc ca nītiyukto na dṛśyate anabhijñaś ca sācivyaṃ gamitaḥ kena hetunā vidyāyukto hy avidyaś ca dhanavān durgatas tathā
english: One who has studied statecraft is not seen acting by its precepts, while the ignorant has been raised to a minister's post—by what cause? And the learned is destitute, while the unlearned is rich.

sanskrit: yadi vidyām upāśritya naraḥ sukham avāpnuyāt na vidvān vidyayā hīnaṃ vṛttyartham upasaṃśrayet
english: If a man could win happiness by leaning on knowledge, then the learned would not, for a livelihood, attach himself to one devoid of learning.

sanskrit: yathā pipāsāṃ jayati puruṣaḥ prāpya vai jalam dṛṣṭārtho vidyayāpy evam avidyāṃ prajahen naraḥ
english: As a man conquers thirst when he has found water, so a man whose aim is fulfilled by knowledge should cast off ignorance.

sanskrit: nāprāptakālo mriyate viddhaḥ śaraśatair api tṛṇāgreṇāpi saṃspṛṣṭaḥ prāptakālo na jīvati
english: He whose time has not come does not die, though pierced by a hundred arrows; but he whose time has come, though touched by only the tip of a blade of grass, does not live.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca īhamānaḥ samārambhān yadi nāsādayed dhanam ugraṃ tapaḥ samārohen na hy anuptaṃ prarohati
english: Bhīṣma said: If, striving through his undertakings, a man does not win wealth, let him mount to fierce austerity; for what is unsown does not sprout.

sanskrit: dānena bhogī bhavati medhāvī vṛddhasevayā ahiṃsayā ca dīrghāyur iti prāhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: By giving one becomes an enjoyer, by service to elders wise, and by non-violence long-lived—so the sages have declared.

sanskrit: tasmād dadyān na yāceta pūjayed dhārmikān api svābhāṣī priyakṛc chuddhaḥ sarvasattvāvihiṃsakaḥ
english: Therefore one should give and not beg, and should honor the righteous, being fair-spoken, doing what is dear, pure, and harming no living creature.

sanskrit: yadā pramāṇaprabhavaḥ svabhāvaś ca sukhāsukhe maśakīṭapipīlānāṃ sthiro bhava yudhiṣṭhira
english: Since the measure and the inborn nature in pleasure and pain are common even to gnats, worms, and ants, be steadfast, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca kāryate yac ca kriyate sac cāsac ca kṛtaṃ tataḥ tatrāśvasīta satkṛtvā asatkṛtvā na viśvaset
english: Bhīṣma said: What is caused to be done and what is done may be good or bad in the doing; therefore, having done good, let one feel assured, but having done evil, let one not feel secure.

sanskrit: kāla evātra kālena nigrahānugrahau dadat buddhim āviśya bhūtānāṃ dharmārtheṣu pravartate
english: It is Time alone here that, granting through time both punishment and grace, enters the minds of beings and sets them moving toward dharma and gain.

sanskrit: yadā tv asya bhaved buddhir dharmyā cārthapradarśinī tadāśvasīta dharmātmādṛḍhabuddhir na viśvaset
english: But when a man's mind becomes righteous and revealing of true gain, then let the righteous-souled one feel assured; one of unsteady mind should not feel secure.

sanskrit: etāvan mātram etad dhi bhūtānāṃ prājñalakṣaṇam kālayukto 'py ubhayavic cheṣam arthaṃ samācaret
english: This much alone is the mark of wisdom in beings: even when bound by time, one who knows both should yet carry out the remaining aim.

sanskrit: yathā hy upasthitaiśvaryāḥ pūjayante narā narān evam evātmanātmānaṃ pūjayantīha dhārmikāḥ
english: For just as men whose lordship has arrived honor other men, so here the righteous honor their own self by their own self.

sanskrit: na hy adharmatayā dharmaṃ dadyāt kālaḥ kathaṃ cana tasmād viśuddham ātmānaṃ jānīyād dharmacāriṇam
english: For Time can in no way render dharma into unrighteousness; therefore one should know the self of a practicer of dharma to be wholly pure.

sanskrit: spraṣṭum apy asamartho hi jvalantam iva pāvakam adharmaḥ satato dharmaṃ kālena parirakṣitam
english: Unrighteousness is unable so much as to touch dharma—ever guarded by Time—as one cannot touch a blazing fire.

sanskrit: kāryāv etau hi kālena dharmo hi vijayāvahaḥ trayāṇām api lokānām ālokakaraṇo bhavet
english: Both these are to be wrought by Time; for dharma is the bringer of victory, and it becomes the light-maker of all the three worlds.

sanskrit: tatra kaś cin nayet prājño gṛhītvaiva kare naram uhyamānaḥ sa dharmeṇa dharme bahubhayacchale
english: Therein some wise man may lead another, taking him by the very hand; himself borne along by dharma, in dharma full of many fears and deceits.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃ śreyaḥ puruṣasyeha kiṃ kurvan sukham edhate vipāpmā ca bhavet kena kiṃ vā kalmaṣanāśanam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What is best for a man here? By doing what does he flourish in happiness? By what does he become free of evil, and what is the destroyer of sin?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ayaṃ daivatavaṃśo vai ṛṣivaṃśasamanvitaḥ dvisaṃdhyaṃ paṭhitaḥ putra kalmaṣāpaharaḥ paraḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: This lineage of the gods, joined with the lineage of seers, recited at the two twilights, my son, is the supreme remover of sin.

sanskrit: devāsuragurur devaḥ sarvabhūtanamaskṛtaḥ acintyo 'thāpy anirdeśyaḥ sarvaprāṇo hy ayonijaḥ
english: The god who is teacher of gods and Asuras, revered by all beings, unthinkable and indefinable, the life of all, born of no womb—

sanskrit: pitāmaho jagannāthaḥ sāvitrī brahmaṇaḥ satī vedabhūr atha kartā ca viṣṇur nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
english: the Grandsire, Lord of the world; Sāvitrī, the true consort of Brahmā; the womb of the Vedas, and the Maker; and Viṣṇu, Lord Nārāyaṇa—

sanskrit: umāpatir virūpākṣaḥ skandaḥ senāpatis tathā viśākho hutabhug vāyuś candrādityau prabhākarau
english: Umā's lord, the odd-eyed one; Skanda the army-commander likewise; Viśākha, the fire that consumes oblations, Vāyu, and the moon and sun, makers of light—

sanskrit: śakraḥ śacīpatir devo yamo dhūmorṇayā saha varuṇaḥ saha gauryā ca saha ṛddhyā dhaneśvaraḥ
english: Śakra the god, lord of Śacī; Yama together with Dhūmorṇā; Varuṇa, and with Gaurī, and with Ṛddhi the lord of wealth—

sanskrit: saumyā gauḥ surabhir devī viśravāś ca mahān ṛṣiḥ ṣaṭkālaḥ sāgaro gaṅgā sravantyo 'tha marudgaṇāḥ
english: the gentle cow, the goddess Surabhī; and Viśravas the great seer; the six seasons, the ocean, the Gaṅgā, the rivers, and then the host of the Maruts—

sanskrit: vālakhilyās tapaḥsiddhāḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanas tathā nāradaḥ parvataś caiva viśvāvasur hahāhuhūḥ
english: the Vālakhilyas, perfected in austerity; Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana likewise; Nārada, and Parvata too; Viśvāvasu, Hāhā and Hūhū—

sanskrit: tumbaruś citrasenaś ca devadūtaś ca viśrutaḥ devakanyā mahābhāgā divyāś cāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ
english: Tumbaru and Citrasena, and the renowned messenger of the gods; the blessed daughters of the gods, and the divine hosts of Apsarases—

sanskrit: urvaśī menakā rambhā miśrakeśī alambuṣā viśvācī ca ghṛtācī ca pañcacūḍā tilottamā
english: Urvaśī, Menakā, Rambhā, Miśrakeśī, Alambuṣā, and Viśvācī, and Ghṛtācī, Pañcacūḍā, Tilottamā—

sanskrit: ādityā vasavo rudrāḥ sāśvinaḥ pitaro 'pi ca dharmaḥ satyaṃ tapo dīkṣā vyavasāyaḥ pitāmahaḥ
english: the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, with the Aśvins, and the ancestors too; Dharma, Truth, Austerity, Consecration, Resolve, the Grandsire—

sanskrit: śarvaryo divasāś caiva mārīcaḥ kaśyapas tathā śukro bṛhaspatir bhaumo budho rāhuḥ śanaiścaraḥ
english: the nights and the days; Mārīca and Kaśyapa likewise; Śukra, Bṛhaspati, Mars, Mercury, Rāhu, and Saturn—
